personality.buyer: Administrators, IT teams, and MSSPs managing firewall logs, compliance, monitoring, and reporting
personality.reasoning: Firewall Analyzer is a security and compliance product for operational IT buyers who value clarity, control, and auditability over decoration. The visual language should feel authoritative and trustworthy, but also highly intelligent and interactive. A compliance-trust direction fits the use case best: structured layouts, sharp typography, dark-led hero treatment, dashboard-inspired sections, and premium data visualization cues. To avoid a generic dark SaaS look, the system should combine deep navy security tones with restrained orange brand energy, layered panels, floating metric chips, and strong contrast between sections. The result should communicate real-time monitoring, forensic depth, and enterprise-grade reliability.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The hero headline is moderately long and should stay authoritative without wrapping awkwardly; 48px balances impact and readability for a security product.

colours.colourReason: Deep navy signals trust, governance, and security authority, while the orange accent preserves Techjockey brand recognition and creates strong CTA contrast. Soft blue-grey backgrounds keep the page premium but not overly heavy.

layout.featureReason: The product has many features, so it should be broken into a spotlight block plus structured grid sections. This allows strong contrast between consecutive sections and makes the monitoring, auditing, and reporting capabilities easier to scan.
layout.darkSectionFor: hero, trust/awards bar, and one mid-page proof section such as compliance or monitoring summary

personality.imageryDirection: Use a layered PNG product dashboard visual on the hero right side, showing firewall logs, rule activity, traffic charts, compliance alerts, and threat indicators. Support with SVG icons for firewall, logs, compliance, monitoring, bandwidth, and policy management. If product screenshots are unavailable, create a CSS-based abstract UI shell with metric cards, live alert pills, and translucent chart panels. Use subtle orange highlights only as an accent, not as the dominant visual field.

Use a restrained credibility strip even without logos: highlight trust through compact badges, compliance cues, and operational proof points. Keep it minimal and calm so it supports rather than competes with the hero.

Break the product content into three alternating modules. Use a spotlight intro panel for each section headline and description, followed by a structured 2-column or 3-column feature grid. For the first section, emphasize firewall compatibility and monitoring. For the second, foreground compliance, configuration auditing, and reporting. For the third, position ROI, productivity, and broad device coverage as business-value cards. Maintain strong whitespace and alternate visual weight between sections for contrast.

If no additional content is available, keep this section out of the main flow or convert it into a small value-props grid only if needed later. Use it as a utility-proof zone with concise cards, but avoid adding unnecessary noise.
Do not introduce self-serve pricing since the reference pattern is lead-gen oriented. Replace with a conversion-oriented qualification card or omit visually until actual pricing content exists.

Use a dark-band testimonial section for contrast and authority. Present the two quotes as premium cards with subtle borders, author titles, and industry labels. Keep typography crisp and highly legible; avoid overly decorative treatment.

Place the lead form as a prominent floating card or split conversion block. Keep fields minimal, with the primary CTA emphasized in solid orange. This should feel like the main conversion anchor after proof and product depth.
If no news or media logos are provided, omit this section or keep it as a lightweight utility strip only. Do not force a marquee when there is no logo content.
